decisions.reason: The single integrated-board topology was already established before this source Event; removing the legacy main-board layer stack adds no topology change.
The removal of the legacy layer stack does not alter the independently specified antenna edge placement, battery-facing orientation, or keepout.
The existing same-message MODIFY already removes obsolete legacy connector-access attributes and records their non-applicability under the integrated architecture.
The existing same-message MODIFY already captures the permitted connector-placement flexibility while preserving the explicit constraints from message 842.
Removing the legacy board's layer-stack requirement does not necessarily cancel or change its separately prepared manufacturing BOM artifact.
Layer-stack removal does not change the integrated design's cost goal, component-selection policy, or connector-reduction strategy.
The source does not determine any change to monitored rails, monitor hardware, measurement coverage, or the unresolved INA omission.
The charge-status display and dedicated LED interface remain valid independently of the removed legacy layer stack.
The source does not change DCDC1 voltage, current rating, regulation behavior, or compensation requirements.
Removing the legacy layer stack does not entail a change to the required panel controls, connector inventory, or signal assignments.
The panel-mounted power-button behavior and PWRON connection are independent of the legacy main-board layer count.
The source does not alter standalone USB power behavior, regulator selection, rail coverage, or source-selection semantics.
